DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix` copies the target file into an empty temporary directory (`tmpdir`) before running static analysis and `test_cmd`.
FOLLOW: Because the patched file is isolated from its project root, sibling modules, and `pyproject.toml`, local imports will fail to resolve. Tools like `pyright` and `mypy` will generate massive false-positive "missing import" errors, causing `net_type_errors` to skyrocket. Furthermore, `test_cmd` run in `tmpdir` will instantly fail because test suites and configurations do not exist there. Every valid fix will be falsely evaluated as `HARMFUL`, breaking the bug-closed gate entirely.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — Mirror the project structure into the sandbox rather than isolating the file. Extract the project root (e.g., the common path of `source_paths`), use `shutil.copytree` to copy it into `tmpdir`, apply the patch to the correct relative path inside the sandbox, and run tools/tests with `cwd` set to the sandbox root.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.85
FLAW_CLASS: 6
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.2
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_apply_fix_to_source` Strategy 2 uses `compile(fix, "<fix>", "exec")` to detect and apply valid whole-file replacements, but does not sanitize markdown code block fences.
FOLLOW: LLMs routinely wrap their proposed code fixes in markdown block markers (e.g., ` ```python `). When `compile()` encounters these backticks, it throws a `SyntaxError`, immediately bypassing Strategy 2. If the regex in the other strategies also fails to match, the valid whole-file fix is silently dropped and evaluated as `UNEVALUABLE`.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — Strip standard markdown code block fences before attempting any patching strategies. Add `fix = re.sub(r"^```[a-zA-Z]*\n|\n```$", "", fix).strip()` right after `fix = proposed_fix.strip()`.
VERIFIED: TRUE
